title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 106
paragraphs: It seems that the extremities of the inhabited world have had the fairest things allotted to them by nature, just as it was the lot of Hellas to have its seasons tempered far more finely than other lands. For first, India is the most distant of inhabited lands towards the East, as I have said a little above; and in this land not only the animals, both birds and four-footed beasts, are much larger than in other places (except the horses, which are surpassed by the Median breed called Nessaian), but also gold is abundant there—some obtained by digging, some brought down by rivers, and some carried off as I have just described. And there the trees that grow wild produce wool that surpasses in beauty and quality that from sheep; and the Indians wear clothing obtained from these trees.
